lastAfter:
The youth's voice rose from the ground where she knelt, thin and cracking like frost on glass. "You twisted it. Your sealed mouth bent the wish toward your own blood."

I opened my mouth to speak the truth of the name she had spoken, the figure that had stepped from the trees wearing a face I once described in private, the way the rite had torn itself sideways before I could stop it. The words died against the weight of every stare. The Dohkar's hands remained lifted, unmoving, as if the air itself might still be mended. Around the clearing the First Favored stood motionless, their Weave-Script flickering in colors that betrayed nothing and everything at once. The youth's coral hair had lost its color at the roots; her aqua skin looked dulled, as if the wish had already begun to claim what it could.

I tried again. "The invocation named something that was not meant to answer. A figure came. It wore the face I—"

"You broke the seal," the youth said. Her small hands pressed against her throat where the color faded. "You flung the band away and called the twist yourself."

The assembly shifted. A low sound moved through them, not quite speech. Two women nearby had already asked whether he was coming. Julian's remembered hand turned the ring on his finger once, thumb and forefinger catching the light that filtered through the leaves above the clearing, the motion slow and anchoring as it always was when he held back what he might have said. I felt the pressure of that remembered stillness between my shoulders even though he stood apart, observing only.

The youth's eyes fixed on me. "You knew the rite could not be touched. You used your sealed mouth anyway."

I shook my head, the motion small. "The name she spoke was not mine. The figure answered it. I tried to stop the final syllable—"

"Enough," one of the Dohkar said, voice low. The word carried the weight of the binding's failure. Every gaze returned to me, and the air between us thickened with the inference already forming. My lineage. The blood that should not have been named here. The unsealed mouth that had broken the circle.

The youth's accusation hung, and the clearing waited for what I would do with it.

Present. The strong, frank face that carried the warmth of a thousand smiles turned toward them, the dark chestnut waves spilling over her shoulders like a living spell, the laugh-lines around her mouth deepening before the low rough laugh escaped, surprising them all.

I realize that old tarot deck is still in my hand. Reassuringly solid. Present. One of the heavy gold cards slips out — "Petition Fate" is inscribed in it. If Fate could reach what the rite refused, I would ask it to take the name the youth spoke and bury it where no one else could hear. No. I would ask it to show me whether the figure truly belonged to the blood I carry, and whether Julian already knows.

ringTail: The youth was sixteen today, old enough to make her first wish under the First Sacrifice rite. The youth lifted her chin and spoke the invocation straight into the clearing air, her voice carrying the name that cracked the rite open. I crossed the circle in two strides and seized her wrist before the final syllable could settle, forcing her gaze back to the prepared altar. A wrong note shivered through every Favored present, their shoulders locking as the mismatch struck their skin. My pulse slammed against my ribs, hot and uneven, while the Dohkar's hands rose in the sudden hush. "Stop," I said, the word scraping out as I yanked the gossamer band free and flung it toward the trees. The twist answered at once. A figure stepped from the shadows wearing the exact face I had once described in private, his eyes sliding past me without recognition. The youth cried out as something tore from her chest, her coral hair bleaching at the roots while the figure turned his back. I stepped between them, one hand lifted to bar his retreat, the other already reaching for the youth's shoulder to anchor what was left. Every eye in the assembly fixed on me. They had watched me break the rite. They had heard the wish name me aloud. Julian's left boot sole rasped once against the root beneath him. The sound pulled my attention sideways for a single heartbeat, his stare pressing between my shoulder blades like a held blade. The youth sank to her knees, one hand at her throat where the color had already begun to fade. I dropped to the ground with her, gripping her elbow to keep her upright, and felt the weight of every inference land on the faces around us. Say it plainly or let the silence finish the work? Julian shifted his weight again, the faint drag of his sole against bark threading through the quiet, and I refused to turn. My hand tightened around my great-grandmother's old tarot deck. I didn't remember bringing it. I toyed with the idea of letting the cards decide.
